rationale: The successor experiment executed in a clean copy (905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8, completed, exit 0) with all fifteen comparisons complete and evaluated: the invocation with a context that never expires stayed pending through a 2000 ms window with leader 1 stable and its payload uncommitted, and once the forced leader change re-armed the gate that same still-pending invocation was admitted with no error and its payload was committed. This update attributes the retained interpretation to that experiment, records the two new observations as durable knowledge, and replaces the two limitations that predicted them but had no retained evidence.

knowledge.statement: With a context that never expires, the same invocation on the re-added voter was still pending after a 2000 ms observation window while leader 1 stayed stable and no node had its payload in committed entries; the invocation was not cancelled by the harness. After a forced campaign made node 2 leader at term 2, that same still-pending invocation was admitted (pending false, returned true, error empty, 3621 ms after it was issued) and its payload was subsequently committed on all three nodes. The pending invocation therefore neither loses its request nor reports an error while it waits; it is held until an observed leader change re-arms the run loop's receive side.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks delivered; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes; witness and retry invocations use bounded contexts while this one uses context.Background and is never cancelled.

interpretations.joint_history: Four receipts from one fixed scenario lineage: 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-experiment (executed as 43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad) and its successors 48ce57b251a644edaaf9d17731df0b25-experiment (a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f), baee4030bf1e4f229c46ece8d0ddc365-experiment (87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4) and de0272862d1842d2af26e89d955ed098-experiment (905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8), each registered with previous_id and a revision_reason. All four build the same configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1 at term 1, apply the same committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes on node 3, use the same witness/control/repair operation ids, payloads, phases, deadlines and windows, and force the same campaign of node 2 into term 2; the successors add event naming, then retry/progress cases, then the context-free case and the post-re-arm observations, without altering the earlier ones. Witnesses agree field for field at the corresponding indices (witness 7/8/9 in all four; control 11/12; repair 15/16, 25/26 or 28/29), so the difference is a property of the fixed scenario rather than of one run.
interpretations.rationale: Four retained executions agree; this revision adds the two observations that were previously only source-derived or seen in a native dry run, and the evidence is otherwise unchanged. In 905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8: node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the admitted witness invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded', 2500 ms), and left its payload absent from every node's committed entries (index 9). During the same stable-leader period the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 14, 15). An invocation issued with a context that never expires was still pending after 2000 ms (index 11: returned false, err empty, voter true, leader 1) with its payload uncommitted (index 12). Two retries on node 3 (indices 20, 25) also did not return and were not committed, while in each interval a proposal by node 2 returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 17, 22). After the forced campaign made node 2 leader at term 2 (index 26) a new invocation returned in 0 ms and committed (indices 28, 29), and the still-pending context-free invocation was admitted (index 30: pending false, returned true, err empty at 3621 ms, leader 2) with its payload then committed on all three nodes (index 31). Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412), so the caller's send on the always non-nil n.propc (node.go:525) stays pending while no leader change is observed, and is admitted unmodified when the gate is re-armed. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader and expects acceptance once a leader is known, which is the condition node 3 satisfies while pending; the control and interval controls exclude cluster-wide stalls, the post-leader-change call excludes a defect in node 3's own state machine, and index 31 shows no work is lost. The defect is therefore the interval itself: a voting member with a known, healthy leader whose proposal duty is held pending without any error signal, for as long as no leadership change is observed, with the requester unable to distinguish this from an ordinary slow proposal.
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised ('propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs'); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.

No work is lost: the pending context-free invocation was admitted unmodified once the gate was re-armed (index 30) and its payload committed (index 31), so the harm is the unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.
The same runs contain successful paths (indices 14, 15, 17, 22, 29), showing proposals are neither generally dropped nor generally blocked.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were 'unknown' because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose has no such gate. No ticks were delivered and delivery was reliable, so no timing or network-fault characterization is claimed; the retry intervals carried no election activity because the harness sends no ticks.

Only the voter-removal form was executed; other transitions that delete the local Progress entry are variants of the same cause and were not executed separately. The same gate also covers Node.ProposeConfChange (node.go:496-502 via stepWithWaitOption), which was not executed.

The retained releases of pending invocations are a caller context deadline (indices 8, 20, 25) and a leader change (index 30); the node-stop exit was not retained after the harness step that mislabelled an already-returned call was removed.

the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
the context-free invocation stayed pending for 2000 ms with leader 1 stable and was admitted with its payload committed only after the leader change
